posts.author: mei
posts.text: Just finished the morning kiosk trial at Raffles Place (40 customers). 19 out of 28 first-time expats and tourists froze for over 2 minutes on Step 2 trying to guess 'Kopi O Kosong' vs 'Kopi C Siew Dai', and 72% missed the tiny language toggle in the corner.

posts.author: arjun
posts.text: Careful with renaming the POS buttons to English though. In POS v2.4, `display_name` prints straight onto the kitchen thermal docket (`ticket_label`). When we tested 'Black Coffee No Sugar' at Tampines, our 65-year-old kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup trying to read the docket.

posts.author: mei
posts.text: Yeah, and Reddit roasted our rival down the street when they renamed Kopi O to 'Local Americano'. Plus the 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page. Let's figure out what to change at the huddle.

posts.author: weiling
posts.text: Our 28 seats were jammed again this morning. Office workers left tissue packets on empty tables before joining the 15-min queue, and 4 laptop freelancers sat across our four 4-seater booths (16 seats) for 2 hours on a single $2.20 Kopi O. That's $420 in lost breakfast sets, and Auntie Mary (62) is still shaken after that guy in a suit yelled at her last week.

posts.author: arjun
posts.text: Those 12 booth wall plugs and the guest Wi-Fi router are wired to our smart relay breaker in the back room, and we still have the numbered table pucks in the storeroom. Let's bring it up in the meeting so we don't put Auntie Mary in the middle.

posts.author: daniel
posts.text: Someone filmed a 74-year-old regular uncle getting turned away at our 'NO CASH ACCEPTED' kiosk sign yesterday and the TikTok clip just hit 40,000 views calling us anti-elderly. 94% of the regulars who walked out only carry $2 and $10 notes, so even a $2.20 Kopi needs change.

posts.author: weiling
posts.text: We can't run cash from the toast counter. Our internal counter hygiene SOP keeps money handling separate from ready-to-eat food: anyone who touches coins or notes has to change gloves and wash hands before slicing kaya toast (+40s per order), and counting cash at night costs $380/month in overtime. Both toast staff are flat out at the 8am queue, Auntie Mary is the only one seating solo diners with hot trays, and there is no spare till or cashier terminal at the front. Physical kiosk bill-acceptors take 3 weeks and $1,400 too.

posts.author: mei
posts.text: I checked our takeaway packaging after @MakanWithZack's 'shrinking butter' TikTok (90k views). Our 12g butter weight didn't shrink at all — it stays thick on dine-in open plates, but sealing cold butter inside a closed takeaway box with hot toast steams and melts half the slab before customers open it.

posts.author: weiling
posts.text: Good catch, because Anchor salted butter jumped 35% last month and doubling our butter slab to 20g across all sets would wipe out $0.42 per set ($1,100/month in margin). Zack wants $600 cash or $450 + 20 Kaya Toast plushies for an 8:30am live re-taste tomorrow, and we only have $750 left in our launch budget.
